label: Rosen (1978), Fundamentals of Measurement and Representation of Natural Systems, §2.9 Appendix, Definition 2.9.1 (book p. 54)
verbatim:
DEFINITION 2.9.1 A system (or formal system) shall consist of a pair (S, F), where S is a set and F is a family of real-valued mappings defined on S. The elements of F will be called the observables of the formal system.
To each formal system defined as above, we can uniquely associate a set of reduced states S/R_F in the fashion we have described in the previous sections; all of the properties we have developed will be meaningful in the context of these formal systems, and we shall use them without further comment.
Notice that we consider two formal systems (S, F) and (S′, F′) as different if S ≠ S′ and/or F ≠ F′.

primitives.scope_note: The first component S of the pair; the carrier whose members the mappings in F are defined on. Rosen assumes no further structure on it.
Used of the members of F: "The elements of F will be called the observables of the formal system."
The form of the system object itself: a system "shall consist of a pair (S, F)". Rosen takes the pairing as given.
The second component F is "a family of real-valued mappings defined on S"; the word is used without further explication.
The members of F: mappings defined on S taking values in the real numbers. Rosen uses the phrase as a primitive ingredient of the pair.
The author's name for the elements of F. Elsewhere in the work Rosen lists "observable" among three basic undefined terms; here it is stipulated as the label for the members of F.
Used in the immediate gloss: to each formal system is uniquely associated "a set of reduced states S/R_F", carried over from the preceding sections.

comment:
DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED
This entry records only that the passage states a definition of "system" at the given locus. No cco is-about relation is asserted between this entry and any subject matter, discipline, or other atlas entry; the catalogue's neutrality invariant forbids inferring topical aboutness from the presence of a definition.

WHAT THE ENCODING LEAVES OUT
The locus is embedded in a longer formal development that the entry does not carry: Definition 2.9.2 (subsystem and extension, S′ ⊆ S and F′ ⊆ F), the remarks that (S, F) is a subsystem of (S, H(S, R)) and that no formal system is a subsystem of (S, ∅), Definition 2.9.3 (morphism as a pair (φ, ψ)), and the closing note that "the class of formal systems becomes a category". Also left out is §2.1's declaration that system, observable and state are three basic undefined terms, together with Propositions 1 and 2, on which Rosen's notion of observable rests; the reduced-state construction S/R_F named in the gloss is developed in earlier sections and is not reproduced here.

CASES
No admits or refuses are recorded: at this locus Rosen offers no example as a system and refuses none. The nearby remark about (S, H(S, R)) and (S, ∅) rules on the subsystem relation, not on systemhood, and so was not treated as a case.

SOURCE FIDELITY
